column1: # BLOB-KIND VECTORS (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §3.1, §6.5; docs/rulings.json
# blob-target-outside-closure-refused). The roots are in
# test/pointer-target-type/blobkind/reader: Text (body *string) and Bin
# (data *bytes), so each root's closure holds ONE blob kind.
# test/pointer-target-type/blobkind/writer is the reader's successor: its Text
# adds a field the reader does not declare, extra *bytes. Every vector is
# written by test/pointer-target-type/blobkind/gen.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   case     what the wire carries
#   unit     the schema directory the root is read against, from the repo root
#   root     the table the wire is read at
#   file     the wire file, in this directory
#   verdict  `read` or `refused`
#   unknown  the report's unknown count, or `-` where the row does not pin one
# The two reserved blob ids are types every reader can name, whatever its root
# reaches: a declared slot naming a blob record of the other kind refuses the
# whole read (wire_damaged, a wrong-type pointer target), and so does a blob
# record no pointer reaches. A blob record of a kind the root's closure lacks,
# named only from a field the reader does not declare (a newer writer's
# field), reads, and counts two `unknown`: the field the reader does not
# declare, and the record it names. A newer writer's TYPE under a declared slot is
# the separate case ../MANIFEST.tsv holds as next-writer-only: it reads, the
# pointer null.
